name: The lodgers of Reconstructed H3 boarding house #01
head: rc_mccarthy_edward

lodging_household.stands_on: The lodging model (T-1370) gives this house an ordinary-night capacity apportioned out of a figure the town model already owns, and the residents layer holds fewer people in it than that. The order book's `lodging` buckets are the quota these people are drawn against.
lodging_household.withdrawn_if: a re-cut lodging model that gives this house a smaller ordinary-night figure, or sources naming the people who actually lodged here; the retirement runs through --build, never by hand
lodging_household.note: BEDS, AND ONE FAMILY. 3 of the people here took a bed and are not kin to each other or to anybody else under this roof — `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one record holds them all. The exception is the keeper and the 2 child(ren) on their card, who are a family and say so: every one of them carries `kin_of` naming the keeper.

household_owed.seated_by: T-1533 (the keeper's children, drawn here), T-1179 (converge)
household_owed.note: DRAWN HERE, AND ONLY THE CHILDREN. The 1840 size histogram draws this keeper a household of 5: the keeper, and 4 child(ren) of whom 2 could be ordered out of the book's `under_10/south/lodging/none` cells. No spouse is drawn — the ledger's `keeper_families` row says why — so this is a FLOOR on the household and not a finished count.

arrival.note: NOT DRAWN HERE, AND THE REASON IS A CIRCLE. The arrival model's own distribution is computed over the compiled scene and the scene carries these cards; an arrival written here would move the table that drew it. The programme's arrival stage owns this block.

basis.note: THE BED IS THE CLAIM. The lodging model puts 12 people in this house on an ordinary night and 28 when it was full, apportioned from the town model's own bracket. These people are here because the beds are, and for no other reason.

replaceable_by.match: sources naming the people who lodged in this house in 1835

works_at.note: Not seated. A lodger's workplace is the business band's (T-1189) and a keeper's premises is the house they are already in.

basis.note: Ordered, not argued: the book counts these people as missing FROM the town of 1 July 1835, so presence is the order rather than a draw made over it.
